mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance, Cap. 37)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For use in Apostille Convention states: Hague Apostille issued by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR. For use in non-Apostille states: Consular Legalization by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs Hong Kong Office and the relevant consulate of the destination state. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General Partner or governing board of the Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Hong Kong notary public, followed by either (a) Hague Apostille for Apostille-jurisdiction counterparties or (b) Consular Legalization for non-Apostille jurisdictions; only one path applies per counterparty.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Limited Partnership Agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign-Invested Partnership and its partners (parallel to articles for corporate entities)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Hong Kong notary public, then either Hague Apostille by the High Court (for Apostille states) or Consular Legalization (for non-Apostille states); the chosen path is final and must not be combined with the other.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued directly by the bank under its official letterhead; for cross-border recognition, the bank's signature is notarized, and the document is then either apostilled by the High Court or consular legalized, depending on the destination state's status as an Apostille member.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening shall be conducted at formation and ongoing on all partners, general partners, ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and directors against: (i) the Hong Kong Police Force's Terrorist Financing and Counter-Terrorism (FTCT) lists; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List; (iv) Her Majesty's Treasury sanctions list; (v) the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's AML/CFT guidance; and (vi) Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) databases. Screening must be evidenced with timestamped screenshots, risk-rated reports, and where a PEP is identified, enhanced due diligence (EDD) including source of wealth/income verification, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. All results must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) - Hong Kong Companies Registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Hong Kong law, a partnership name may be registered in English and/or Chinese. An English name must not consist solely of Chinese characters; a Chinese name may be in traditional characters. There is no statutory transliteration device; a Chinese name may be adopted if it is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing name and does not constitute an offence. The four-tier naming structure used in mainland China is not applicable in the Hong Kong SAR.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal, the applicant may make a written request for reconsideration to the Hong Kong Companies Registry Registrar within 30 days of the notice of refusal, setting out grounds and paying the reconsideration fee (if any). The Registrar will review the name against the statutory criteria under section 100 of Cap. 622 (or Cap. 37 for partnerships). If the reconsideration fails, the applicant may either re-submit with a modified name or file an appeal to the Court of First Instance by way of judicial review within 3 months, following Order 53 of the Rules of the High Court. In urgent cases, an inter partes summons may be issued. Legal advice should be sought regarding the prospects of success.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For Hong Kong, a registered office for a limited partnership must be a physical location in Hong Kong capable of receiving service of process. A virtual office or commercial mailbox may be accepted if it is a genuine, staffed physical address and the service provider contracts to receive and forward documents. However, the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and banks may view a virtual office with low substance as high risk; for an AI LLM API platform with cryptocurrency payment rails, an independent bank may require a lease or serviced office agreement, company letterhead, and a physical presence of the General Partner. Virtual office is not statutorily prohibited, but a pure PO Box is likely rejected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The risk of an unannounced physical inspection by the Companies Registry, IRD, or HKPF is approximately 8% per annum for a low-risk AI API token provider. Essential operational checklist: (1) a visible signage or directory listing; (2) a secured mailbox; (3) the capacity to accept and acknowledge service of process; (4) retention of statutory books, partnership records, and accounting documents at the registered office or at an approved location; (5) current Business Registration Certificate displayed; (6) proof of coverage for in-person inspection by the registered office service provider. Maintaining a virtual office with a full-time receptionist can mitigate the risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 1997, revised 2006), Articles 2, 8, 9, 14, 16, 17, 22, 23, 62 and 63; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 4, 28, 30 and 31; Administrative Measures for the Establishment of Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprises (Order No. 2 [2010] of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce and the Ministry of Commerce), Articles 2, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10; where the investing partner is a Hong Kong entity, also the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) and Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38) for authorization evidence and legalization.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), acting through the local Market Supervision Administration at the registered place and its Government Affairs Service Center; the Hong Kong Companies Registry is separately engaged only for issuing certificate of good standing and entity authorization records of the Hong Kong investing partner.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Enterprise Registration Application Form, together with the duly executed Partnership Agreement, capital contribution schedule, foreign partner qualification documents, and registered office address proof, submitted under the Administrative Measures for the Establishment of Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Foreign-Invested Partnership has no statutory minimum registered capital, no minimum paid-up capital, and no blocked escrow account requirement under PRC partnership law. Partners determine the amount, form, and schedule of contributions in the Partnership Agreement; contributions may be made in cash, in-kind assets, intellectual property, or technology. Any foreign-currency capital contribution remitted from Hong Kong must be received through a bank undertaking Foreign Exchange registration under SAFE rules, but this is a foreign-exchange compliance condition and not a capital lock-up.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; electronic portal: eTAX (https://www.etax.gov.hk) including the Business Registration Office e-services
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) in the Hong Kong SAR, the statutory tax identifier is the Business Registration Number (BRN) issued by the Business Registration Office of the IRD under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310). The process is: (1) file Form IRBR 1 - Application for Business Registration within one month of commencement of business via the eTAX portal or in hard copy; (2) submit the partnership agreement, identification documents for each general and limited partner, and evidence of the local registered business address; (3) where the partnership has no physical presence in Hong Kong, appoint a Hong Kong resident agent or law firm to receive official correspondence and service of documents; (4) obtain the Business Registration Certificate and use the BRN as the partnership's TIN for all tax correspondence, customs/trade declarations, and banking records. No separate VAT or GST identification number exists in Hong Kong. The partnership itself is transparent for profits tax; each partner is separately assessed on their Hong Kong-source share of partnership profits and, where required, the partner provides their home jurisdiction TIN in filing documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Hong Kong does not operate a check-the-box or entity classification election; a partnership is automatically treated as transparent under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112). Eligible partners may elect personal assessment under Part VII of the Inland Revenue Ordinance for their partnership profits. No hybrid mismatch election is available under Hong Kong law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No indirect tax (no VAT, GST, or sales and use tax is levied in Hong Kong)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable. Hong Kong has no VAT/GST registration threshold because no such indirect tax exists. Under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), any person, including a partnership, carrying on business in Hong Kong must apply for business registration within one month of commencement of business, irrespective of turnover, unless a statutory exemption applies. The Business Registration Certificate and BRN are used for tax administration rather than indirect tax collection.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Not applicable. Hong Kong does not mandate electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API integration, anti-fraud digital stamping, or a national e-invoicing clearance platform for indirect tax purposes. For profits tax recordkeeping, taxpayers may use commercial invoices, contracts, bank statements, and other business records; the IRD does not prescribe a statutory e-invoice XML schema.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. Hong Kong imposes no VAT/GST on exports, so there is no 0% export VAT rate to substantiate. The cross-border supply of AI/LLM API platform services from Hong Kong has no indirect tax consequence. For direct tax purposes, if the FIP seeks to treat the profits as non-Hong Kong-source (offshore), it must demonstrate under the source principles in the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) that the essential profit-generating operations and contracts were performed outside Hong Kong. No zero-rating certificate or export VAT form is issued by the IRD.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable for VAT. For goods exported from Hong Kong, where a declaration is required, lodge a Hong Kong Export Declaration (Form 2) through the Trade and Industry Department's electronic platform via Government Electronic Trading Services (GETS) or the Trade Single Window in accordance with the Import and Export (Registration) Ordinance (Cap. 60).
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Hong Kong.
Sales contract, service agreement, or API license/subscription order showing supply to a non-Hong Kong customer.
Bank credit advice, payment settlement records, and foreign currency receipt evidence; nothing equivalent to an Inward Remittance Certificate is issued or required in Hong Kong.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT clawback can arise because Hong Kong has no VAT/GST. However, the IRD may rigorously audit an offshore profits claim on export income; if the taxpayer cannot substantiate that the profits are sourced outside Hong Kong, additional profits tax may be assessed. Under section 82A of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, a person who without reasonable excuse makes an incorrect return or statement may be liable to a penalty not exceeding three times the amount of tax undercharged, plus fixed penalties and possible prosecution for fraud. False trade declarations made under the Import and Export (Registration) Ordinance (Cap. 60) are criminal offences and may expose the FIP and its partners to fines and imprisonment. No retrospective VAT clawback is applicable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), empowered by the People's Bank of China (PBOC); for the Hong Kong leg, Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) operates the Linked Exchange Rate System with no foreign exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a current-account convertible regime: genuine trade and service payments can be settled by authorized banks after verification, but capital account transactions require SAFE registration, quota, or specific approval. The Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) may receive foreign currency capital contributions from Hong Kong partners, but the funds must enter through a SAFE-registered capital project account and may be converted into RMB only after the bank verifies the underlying FDI record. RMB conversion is not unconditional: the settlement proceeds must be used for the FIP's approved business purposes, cannot flow into prohibited sectors such as unlicensed securities investment or speculative real estate, and cannot be used to repay domestic RMB loans in a manner that violates SAFE circulars. Profit remittance to non-resident partners is generally permitted after an annual audit, tax clearance, and a certified public accountant statement of distributable profits, but pass-through taxation under the partnership regime may impose withholding obligations on Chinese-source income attributable to non-resident partners. The Hong Kong jurisdiction is fully convertible, with the HKD pegged in the 7.75 to 7.85 range against the USD and no surrender or approval requirements for dividends, trade receipts, or capital returns. The practical friction is therefore concentrated in the PRC capital account, not in Hong Kong convertibility, and requires tight documentary alignment before any cross-border movement of funds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the 2012 PRC foreign exchange reform, the mandatory surrender ratio for export proceeds is effectively zero; exporters are not required to convert foreign currency into RMB. However, all overseas export/service receipts must be repatriated into mainland China, and the statutory benchmarking period for goods export proceeds is generally 180 days from the date of customs declaration. Service trade income, including AI and software API fees, may be retained in a foreign exchange settlement account or converted at the bank's spot rate, provided the underlying contract, invoices, and tax certificates are available. Surplus foreign currency retained beyond the designated account limit must be reported to SAFE through the bank's foreign exchange monitoring system, and any conversion into RMB is voluntary. Hong Kong imposes no surrender rule for export proceeds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to conditional-low for the PRC FIP. Offshore digital EMIs such as Stripe, Wise, and Revolut Business are not legally authorized to open principal settlement accounts for enterprises in mainland China or to process CNY clearing through PBOC's payments system. Stripe may operate only as a front-end card acceptance gateway at the Hong Kong treasury node if the underlying funds settle to a fully licensed Hong Kong bank and are subsequently remitted to the FIP through SWIFT. Cryptocurrency-denominated USDC settlement is not viable for the PRC FIP's books; the Hong Kong node may convert USDC to HKD/USD through a licensed Hong Kong virtual-asset service provider, after which only fiat HKD/USD may be transferred onshore. The FIP should therefore treat domestic Tier-1 banks as the mandatory backbone and fintech EMIs as auxiliary invoicing tools, not as regulated banking rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory general partners and the FIP's senior compliance officer must physically attend an in-branch KYC interview at the opening mainland bank. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for a PRC Foreign-Invested Partnership because SAFE and the bank's Article IX clearing rules require physical verification of signatures and ultimate beneficial ownership. For Hong Kong partners, an initial identity interview may be conducted at a major Hong Kong banking office under a joint KYC arrangement, but the FIP itself must still complete an onshore in-branch interview. All Hong Kong corporate documents must be authenticated with Hong Kong notary public or CPA certification, and where required, legalized, before the mainland branch will approve the relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Partnership opacity: HK limited partnership layers hide the natural persons holding more than 10% economic interest in the FIP, with no clear source-of-wealth trail for the foreign capital contribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership chart from the FIP to each ultimate natural person; Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate and Certificate of Incorporation; notarized partnership agreement with economic split; signed UBO declarations; passport copies; source-of-wealth statements covering at least 12 months; negative PEP findings; bank reference letters from the HK investor's existing bank; and a signed declaration that no sanctioned individual or entity is a partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business description mismatch: the AI/LLM API platform has no audited revenue, no physical operating base in the PRC, and target payment rails include Stripe and USDC, creating a high-risk inference that the FIP is an unlicensed payment or money transmission conduit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed customer API subscription agreements; commercial invoices and billing schedules; data-center and cloud-hosting contracts; privacy policy and PIPL compliance note; board resolution approving only fiat banking rails; a formal prohibition on accepting anonymous crypto payments; the platform's AML manual; business plan showing model licensing and inference token sales; and a CPA's letter confirming the intended revenue recognition treatment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SAFE capital injection mismatch: the incoming SWIFT remitter may not exactly match the partner name in the SAFE FDI registration, or the applicable foreign exchange purpose code is missing, triggering an automated discrepancy and a rejected capital project deposit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI registration receipt; SAMR-issued Foreign-Invested Partnership certificate; latest partnership registration list naming the exact HK partner; board or partner meeting resolution approving the capital call; remittance instruction template using the bank-designated SAFE purpose code for partnership capital contribution; source-of-funds records from the HK remitting bank; and a signed indemnity confirming that no undisclosed nominee is funding the contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential profit-stripping or disguised dividend distribution: the FIP attempts to repatriate profits or return capital to HK partners before completing annual audits, tax clearance, and capital maintenance checks, which can be classified as unlawful offshore profit shifting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CPA-audited annual financial statements for the FIP; PRC tax clearance certificate or payment vouchers for withholding taxes; partner meeting minutes approving the profit distribution; capital maintenance calculation under PRC partnership law; transfer pricing documentation for related-party service fees; outstanding tax verification from the tax bureau; and a sworn statement that the distribution does not breach solvency or creditor protection rules.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The HK partner should execute a SWIFT MT103 or, for larger HKD transfers, a HKD CHATS settlement instruction from its licensed HK bank account to the FIP's SAFE-registered Capital Project Foreign Exchange Account at Bank of China Limited, ICBC, China Construction Bank, or China Merchants Bank. The remittance must name the FIP as beneficiary, the registered HK partner as remitter, and use the bank-approved SAFE purpose code for foreign direct investment capital contribution, generally referenced as SAFE transaction code 601 for FDI equity or partnership capital. The bank will require the SAFE FDI registration receipt, the FIP's partnership certificate, the capital contribution schedule, and an internal instruction letter before crediting the account. After receipt, the bank initiates capital verification through the SAFE FDI reporting system and a licensed CPA issues or updates the capital verification statement. RMB settlement from the capital project account is permitted only after the bank files a settlement-under-capital-project entry and verifies that the funds are deployed for the FIP's approved AI/LLM API business operations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Recurring AI API subscription fees from overseas customers should be repatriated via SWIFT MT103 with the correct service trade purpose code, supported by commercial invoices and the completed SAFE current-account verification declaration. For large customized AI model deployment contracts, a Commercial Letter of Credit can be used when the contract has measurable delivery/acceptance milestones and verifiable software export documentation. Documentary Collections, including D/P and D/A, are suitable for maintenance renewals, model version releases, and milestone-based licensing instalments where the counterparty requires shipment evidence. The FIP must do all onshore outbound settlement through direct member bank clearing and cannot route USDC or other crypto directly through the mainland banking system. The Hong Kong treasury node may convert USDC to HKD/USD through a licensed Hong Kong VASP and then transmit via CHATS/SWIFT to the mainland bank for onshore conversion.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY/USD forward contracts are permitted onshore with a genuine underlying trade or capital exposure, typically with a tenor up to 12 months and a hedge ratio not exceeding 100% of the committed receipts or payments.
Offshore non-deliverable forwards in offshore CNY (CNH/USD NDF) are permissible only for the Hong Kong treasury node, not for the PRC FIP; onshore NDFs are not permitted in mainland China.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps are permissible only when a real debt or cross-border financing flow exists, such as a HK partner term loan converted into RMB, and the notional amount must match the underlying contract, require board approval, and be recorded with SAFE where applicable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the expiry date shown on the current Business Registration Certificate; the Inland Revenue Department issues a renewal demand notice approximately one month before expiry, and payment must be made no later than the expiry date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts an additional late fee of HK$300. Operating without a valid Business Registration Certificate is an offence punishable by a fine of up to HK$5,000 and on continued default a daily fine of HK$200 per day; prosecution may follow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for Partnership (Form BIR52)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the date of issue of the return. For the year of assessment ending 31 March, the Inland Revenue Department normally issues BIR52 on the first working day of April, with a statutory deadline of 30 April unless a specifically granted extension applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse: fine of up to HK$10,000 and a further daily fine of HK$300 for continued default. In cases of understatement or evasion, a penalty not exceeding 100% of the tax undercharged may be imposed, with criminal prosecution in serious cases.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (Forms BIR56A and BIR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the issue date of the return, normally 1 April through 30 April for the relevant year of assessment ended 31 March; this obligation applies only if the partnership employs individuals.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without reasonable excuse: fine of up to HK$10,000 plus a daily penalty of HK$300 for each day the failure continues; false declarations may result in prosecution and additional tax penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notification of Changes to Limited Partnership Particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 days after any change in the general partner, limited partners, capital contributions, firm name, registered office address, or any other registered particulars of the limited partnership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a change notice without lawful excuse renders the partnership and its general partner liable to a fine not exceeding HK$5,000, with a further daily fine for continued non-compliance after conviction.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Hong Kong partnership is not automatically subject to a statutory audit solely because of balance sheet size, turnover, or headcount. However, the Inland Revenue Department may require a certified public accountant to audit the partnership's financial statements under section 51C of the Inland Revenue Ordinance where the annual turnover exceeds HK$5,000,000, where the tax return is selected for investigation, or where the partnership's accounts are considered necessary to verify assessable profits. For any associated Hong Kong private company, statutory audit becomes mandatory unless the company satisfies at least two of the three small-company exemption thresholds: total annual revenue not exceeding HK$20,000,000; total assets not exceeding HK$20,000,000; and average number of employees not exceeding 100. Where the audit mandate applies, the auditor shall be a Hong Kong certified public accountant licensed under the Professional Accountants Ordinance.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), fully converged with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB. Partnerships not required to apply full IFRS may, where permitted by the HKICPA, apply Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards for Private Entities (HKFRS-PE). Tax computations must follow the Inland Revenue Ordinance and relevant Inland Revenue Department interpretations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not maintain a public annual UBO filing requirement for ordinary partnerships. For a limited partnership, the general partner must ensure that the Companies Registry is notified within 7 days of any change in partner identity or capital contribution. Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance, the licensed corporate service provider must conduct client due diligence on beneficial owners at onboarding, on material changes, and on a risk-sensitive periodic basis; an annual KYC re-verification of beneficial owners is recommended standard practice. Any shareholding or partnership-interest transfer that changes the partner registry must be recorded in the partnership register and, where applicable, notified to the Inland Revenue Department and the Companies Registry within the relevant statutory deadline. There is no separate cascading UBO confirmation form submitted to the Hong Kong Government for a partnership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners with capital contributions and profit-sharing ratios
Register of General Partner(s) and/or Managing Partner(s)
Register of Charges/Mortgages created over partnership assets
Minute Book of partner meetings and management committee decisions
Beneficial Ownership and AML/KYC Register maintained by the licensed corporate service provider

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 1,200 per annum for a Hong Kong registered office, partnership agent, and corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 5,000 per annum for a Hong Kong certified public accountant audit of a partnership, depending on transaction volume, number of partners, and the scope of the Inland Revenue Department or partnership agreement requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The FIP is a pass-through entity for PRC Enterprise Income Tax (CIT); the 25% statutory rate applies at the level of a corporate partner on its distributive share. Incentives available to the underlying AI business include: 15% preferential rate for a qualifying High and New Technology Enterprise; 10% rate for a key software enterprise; 100% additional deduction for qualified R&D expenses; and free-trade-zone or Shenzhen Qianhai / Hainan free-zone incentives that may reduce the effective rate to 15% for encouraged industries. These incentives are claimed by the corporate partner, not by the partnership itself.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Partnership Annual Income-Aggregation and Allocation Statement (Part A of the PRC Partnership Tax Pass-Through Report), filed through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax platform (do not use Form A100000 for the FIP itself).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal-year basis), in parallel with the partners' own CIT/IIT filings
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the close of the fiscal year (generally by May 31 of the following calendar year).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include China-source revenue from APIs consumed by industrial customers physically located in mainland China. For cross-border e-commerce or API resellers, identify whether the non-resident has a PE through a dependent agent before attributing profit.
Do not apply a routine mark-up to a related offshore compute provider without a Transfer Pricing policy; these costs must be supported by invoices, contracts and an allocation key.

For any HK-based algorithm engineers, notify the tax authority if services are performed partly in mainland China; the 183-day employment exemption under the DTA must be supported by a payroll analysis.

Net profit after statutory adjustments, including add-backs for non-deductible entertainment and advertising expenses. Any losses allocated to a non-resident partner cannot be offset against their other China income unless the partner has a PE in China; retain the calculation schedule.
Pro-rata share credited to a mainland corporation (25% CIT). The partner picks the share into A100000 line 30; the FIP does not pay CIT on this share.

This share is subject to withholding at the statutory 10% unless a DTA rate reduction is substantiated; the FIP acts as withholding agent and must remit tax within 7 days of allocation or payment, whichever is earlier.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Partnership Return carries a RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 fine, rising to RMB 50,000 in serious cases under TCAL Art. 62. Understated pass-through income may be recharacterized as tax evasion, attracting a 50% to 5x penalty (TCAL Art. 63), a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%, and, for criminal fraudulent allocations, reference PRC Criminal Law Art. 201.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: A100000 - Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return (A-type) filed by the mainland corporate partner of the FIP through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual reconciliation, with quarterly provisional CIT prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return within 5 months after fiscal year-end (by May 31); quarterly prepayments within 15 days after each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales revenue of the corporate partner itself
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not consolidate FIP revenue as sales; the FIP is a separate pass-through entity under Cai Shui [2008] No. 159.
Start from the partner's statutory financial statements and add back any accounting provisions not recognized for CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net partnership income allocated from FIP
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add or subtract the partner's distributive share of FIP taxable income as shown on the Partnership Allocation Statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deductible items and R&D super-deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 100% additional deduction for qualified AI R&D costs only to the partner's eligible expenditure traceable through the FIP.
Use 25% unless the partner satisfies the 15% High and New Technology Enterprise or 10% Key Software Enterprise conditions; attach certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT payable and foreign tax credit settlement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the FIP is taxed abroad or the partner claims credit for HK tax, complete the foreign tax credit schedule and attach the relevant Tax Payment Certificates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or false filing of A100000 triggers TCAL Art. 62/63: an immediate fine up to RMB 50,000 and a tax evasion penalty from 50% to 5x of the underpaid CIT; willful non-filing with underpaid tax exceeding RMB 100,000 is a criminal threshold under PRC Criminal Law Art. 201.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Non-Resident Enterprise Income Tax Withholding Return (NR-EIT-WHT Return / Form FQN010), filed on the e-Tax portal by the withholding agent, which is the FIP itself for profit allocations to non-resident partners.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Event-driven, transaction-based for each distribution, interest, royalty, or profit remittance; no annual filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 7 days from the date of withholding, which is the earlier of actual payment, book entry, or deemed allocation deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State each non-resident partner's legal name, jurisdiction of tax residence, treaty residence, and copy of the Certificate of Resident Status.
Classify as business profit distribution from FIP, interest, royalty, or other income; the DTA treatment differs for each category.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income amount and tax base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the gross allocated share before any deductions; for royalty and interest, use the gross amount paid or credited.
Apply 10% if no treaty relief is claimed; ensure the income is not allocable to a PE maintained by the non-resident in mainland China.

Insert the claimed reduced rate: 5% for qualified Hong Kong corporate dividend/profit beneficiary, 7% for interest, and 5% or 7% for royalties; attach beneficial ownership substantiation and the HK Certificate of Resident Status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: WHT remittance and proof of payment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the tax to the State Taxation Administration treasury within the 7-day window and file the electronic remittance voucher; late remittance triggers daily surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold makes the withholding agent liable for the tax, late-payment surcharge, and a fine from 50% to 5x of the un-withheld amount under TCAL Art. 69; false beneficial-ownership claims may trigger treaty denial, additional 10% WHT, and criminal charges for fraudulent refund claims.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (PRC EIT Law Art. 37 and Art. 3(3)); for a Foreign-Invested Partnership, allocation of China-source operational profit to a non-resident partner is treated as a profit share subject to 10% final withholding, regardless of the partnership's pass-through status.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the Mainland China-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement: (1) Obtain from the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department a Certificate of Resident Status (COR/TRC) confirming the partner's Hong Kong tax residence; (2) Prepare a Beneficial Ownership declaration with legal, business and bank substantiation showing the partner has not merely routed the income to a third-country resident; (3) Submit the COR, ownership chart, and DTA claim form to the FIP (withholding agent) before or at the time of profit allocation; (4) The withholding agent applies the reduced rate, where permitted, and files the NR-EIT-WHT Return; (5) If the tax authority refuses the reduced rate, the non-resident partner must pay the 10% statutory WHT and file a tax treaty relief refund claim under STA Announcement [2019] No. 35. Because partnership interests are not corporate shares, the 5% DWT rate in Article 10 of the Mainland-HK Arrangement usually applies only where the partnership profit share is economically equivalent to a dividend from an enterprise in which the Hong Kong partner holds at least 25% of the capital.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory China WHT on outbound interest and royalties is 10% (EIT Law Art. 37). Under the Mainland-HK DTA: interest is capped at 7%; royalties are capped at 5% for literary, artistic and cinematographic copyrights and 7% for patents, trademarks and know-how, subject to beneficial-ownership and anti-abuse provisions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File threshold: annual controlled tangible-asset transactions exceeding RMB 200 million, intangible-asset/royalty/financial transactions exceeding RMB 100 million, or other controlled-services transactions exceeding RMB 40 million (STA Announcement [2016] No. 42). Master File threshold: group-wide related-party revenue above RMB 1 billion with associated-party transactions; contemporaneous TP documentation must be submitted with the annual CIT package (Form A100000 plus related-party forms G100000 and schedules).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The FIP and its HK partner must demonstrate real personnel, premises, decision-making and risk-bearing capacity under China's General Anti-Avoidance Rule (EIT Law Art. 47) and the Beneficial Owner substance-over-form checks. Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) for an AI LLM API platform include model training, fine-tuning, API pricing, customer contract execution, billing and risk management; these cannot be delegated to a shell affiliate merely to claim treaty benefits or offshore profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - Fraudulent Pass-Through Allocation and WHT Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP records a 90% management service fee payable to an ostensibly unrelated Hong Kong affiliate, strips taxable profit, and simultaneously fails to withhold statutory 10% WHT on profits allocated to non-resident partners; the China tax authority is never informed of the HK affiliate's common ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TCAL Art. 63 imposes recovery of underpaid tax plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% and a fine from 50% to 5 times the evaded tax; TCAL Art. 69 makes the FIP, as withholding agent, liable for the uncollected WHT; PRC Criminal Law Art. 201 creates a criminal threshold at RMB 100,000 of avoided tax or 10% of tax payable for the filing year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are personally liable if they knew of and directed the false allocation; the corporate veil is pierced under Company Law Art. 20, exposing personal assets; civil asset restitution is ordered by the tax authority; a departure-restriction travel ban or blacklisting is imposed on the legal representative and directors; and in aggravated cases the directors face imprisonment up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Treaty Abuse (Beneficial Ownership Fraud)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong parent partner has a registered address, one local nominee director, no telephone line, no AI/LLM technical staff, no board minutes, and its entire revenue is immediately on-paid to the mainland founders; it is inserted solely to lower the Chinese withholding tax from 10% to a 5% dividend rate under the Hong Kong-Mainland Tax Arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty benefits under STA Announcement [2019] No. 35, followed by a final withholding assessment at the statutory 10%; Hong Kong IRD may withdraw the Certificate of Resident Status where the company is not managed and controlled in Hong Kong; mainland penalties under TCAL Art. 44 for failure to supply information and a fine up to RMB 50,000 are also triggered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of both the Hong Kong nominee company and the mainland GP are exposed to piercing of the corporate veil; the nominee director's signature on false beneficial-ownership declarations is a criminal false statement offence under HK Crimes Ordinance Cap. 200 s. 36, carrying imprisonment up to 14 years; mainland-based directors are placed on the tax debt blacklist, subject to travel bans and asset freezes until the underpaid 10% WHT plus penalties are settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP sells AI API tokens to a related Hong Kong marketing vehicle at a 3% gross margin, while the Hong Kong vehicle resells to global customers at a 40% margin; no contemporaneous TP Local File or Master File has been prepared, and the transfer price is not supported by a value-chain contribution or profit split analysis, effectively transferring intangible value to the HK entity without CIGA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC EIT Law Art. 41 mandates arm's length adjustments; the tax authority may reattribute profits and impose 100% of the profit adjustment plus interest; TCAL Art. 32 imposes a 0.05% daily late-payment interest on underpaid tax for the years under audit; TCAL Art. 63 adds a 50% to 5x civil penalty; deliberate falsification of contemporaneous documents may be treated as tax fraud under criminal law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or signed the artificial pricing are accessories to the tax evasion; they may be required to pay compensation for the company's shortfall under Company Law Art. 21 and Art. 20 veil-piercing rules; a travel ban and blacklist are imposed on all directors, officers and beneficial owners in the tax enforcement stage; if convicted, the sentencing range for fraudulent transfer pricing is imprisonment up to 3 years where the evasion exceeds the criminal threshold and 3 to 7 years where the amount is major (PRC Criminal Law Art. 201).
